bundleNote: A bundle is a whole pre-vetted pairing: the three models AND the operating point measured for that combination. The threshold is not a property of the embedder alone - segment length moves it as much as the model does (CAM++ measured 0.30 on 1-2s utterances and 0.68 on 5-20s ones), so an operating point is only meaningful for a stated pairing and utterance-length floor. A bundle with no speakerThreshold has never been calibrated here; the engine then withholds speaker labels until a deployment calibrates its own, which is the honest failure rather than guessing.

bundles.name: Nemotron streaming + TitaNet-small (accuracy-first, NVIDIA licence)
bundles.licenceSummary: NVIDIA Open Model License (ASR) + CC-BY-4.0 (speaker) + MIT (segmentation)
bundles.notes: The pairing validated on real meetings, and the only one demonstrated end to end on a live multi-speaker call. NOT redistributable: the ASR weights are under the NVIDIA Open Model License. Threshold measured across two meetings; different speakers scored at most 0.107 in one and 0.307 in another, so 0.4 clears the harder pair rather than the easier one. Known weakness: under-splits a channel dominated by one talker - on a 31-minute three-person call the quieter tab voice took 13 rows against roughly 41 expected.

bundles.name: Zipformer + WeSpeaker CAM++ (Apache-2.0 and MIT only)
bundles.notes: Redistributable, and worse. The ASR model is trained on LibriSpeech read speech, so expect degraded text on spontaneous meeting audio; the embedder's measured margin is 0.143 against TitaNet's 0.43 on identical audio, and a different speaker once reached 0.761 against a same-speaker floor of 0.763. 0.68 holds only for utterances of roughly 5s and up, which is why minSegmentMs matters more here than elsewhere.

bundles.name: Nemotron streaming, no diarization
bundles.notes: Smallest image and lowest latency for a deployment that wants an alternative to Amazon Transcribe but labels transcripts by audio channel. Diarization requests are reported as unsupported rather than silently returning no labels.

models.name: icefall streaming Zipformer English (int8, Apache-2.0)
models.note: Fully permissive alternative to the NVIDIA-licensed default: Apache-2.0 weights from icefall, so an Apache-2.0-only deployment can pair it with a WeSpeaker embedder. Trained on LibriSpeech read speech, so expect worse accuracy on real meeting audio (noise, cross-talk, spontaneous speech) than the Nemotron default; unmeasured here.

speakerModels.name: NVIDIA TitaNet-small speaker embedding (192-dim)
speakerModels.measured: 2026-08-12, native 16 kHz meeting audio: same-speaker cosine median 0.25-0.51 (p5 0.099), different-speaker median -0.02 (p95 0.074, max 0.107). 2026-08-15, a second meeting with 7-20s utterances: same-speaker 0.74-0.91, and two similar-sounding women scored 0.246-0.307 between them while a third, very different voice scored -0.07 to 0.10 against both. Two lessons: same-speaker scores rise sharply once short utterances are filtered out (min_segment_ms), and how far apart two DIFFERENT speakers land depends on the pair - 0.107 for one pair, 0.307 for another - so a threshold has to clear the hardest pair it will meet, not the easiest one it was measured on.

speakerModels.name: WeSpeaker CAM++ (large-margin), English
speakerModels.measured: 2026-08-12, utterances of 1-2s: same-speaker median 0.27, different-speaker median 0.30 (p95 0.53) - overlapping. 2026-08-19, the same voices with 5-20s utterances: same-speaker 0.763-0.872, different-speaker 0.407-0.621 within a channel, a gap of 0.143, so 0.68 works. Segment length moves this model's operating point as much as the model choice does. Caveat: across channels a different speaker reached 0.761, which nearly touches the same-speaker floor, so the margin is thinner than TitaNet's 0.43 on identical audio.

speakerModels.name: WeSpeaker ResNet293 (large-margin), English
speakerModels.measured: NOT RECOMMENDED. 2026-08-19, real meeting audio: same-speaker 0.962-0.986 but different speakers 0.886-0.921, so the distributions overlap and no threshold separates them - 0.8 merged every voice on a channel into one. Everything recorded through the same path scores 0.88+ regardless of who is speaking while cross-channel pairs sit at 0.55-0.63, which suggests it encodes the recording condition more than the voice. Earlier note (2026-08-12) already showed overlapping tails; this quantifies it. No recommendedThreshold is shipped because there is no honest value.

speakerModels.name: No speaker model (transcription only, no diarization)

thresholdNote: recommendedThreshold is per model and NOT interchangeable: cosine similarity scales differ between embedders. Changing the speaker model without re-measuring its operating point will either fragment one speaker into many or merge several into one.

segmentationModels.name: pyannote segmentation 3.0 (speaker turn and overlap detection)
segmentationModels.note: Converted to ONNX by k2-fsa from the gated pyannote/segmentation-3.0 weights and redistributed ungated with the upstream MIT licence file, so no Hugging Face token is needed. Detects speaker turns and overlap inside one endpointed utterance, which raw embeddings cannot do reliably at short durations.

segmentationModels.name: No turn detection (one speaker per endpointed utterance)
